Messages.Author: guntherbl
Messages.Body:
Please help me understand these two abilities:
Jacko (Brujah-Antitribu)
Card text says:Jacko gets an optional additional strike during the first
round of combat. This does not count against his additional strike effect
limit for that round.
What is an "additional strike effect limit"? How and when is it
determined?

Genevieve (Gangrel-Antitribu)
"Genevieve gets one additional vote during each political action"
She is a Priscus so when is her additional vote cast: during the Prisci
sub-referendum or during the main referendum?

By the way: You can't play a press after S:CE, right?

Thank you.

Messages.Author: John Whelan
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 8 Oct 2000, guntherbl wrote:

> Please help me understand these two abilities:
> Jacko (Brujah-Antitribu)
> Card text says:Jacko gets an optional additional strike during the first
> round of combat. This does not count against his additional strike effect
> limit for that round.
> What is an "additional strike effect limit"? How and when is it
> determined?

You may use only one source of additional strikes per round. Jacko's
special text would count (preventing him from playing any additional
strike cards), if it were not for the card text saying otherwise. As it
stands, he could play "Blur" *and* use his special ability to gain a total
of three additional strikes per round.

> Genevieve (Gangrel-Antitribu)
> "Genevieve gets one additional vote during each political action"
> She is a Priscus so when is her additional vote cast: during the Prisci
> sub-referendum or during the main referendum?

She votes during the main referendum. Her special ability is distinct
from that of Gratiano, who gains an additional vote during the Prisci sub
vote.

> By the way: You can't play a press after S:CE, right?

No, you can't.

(As an aside, though, I think that allowing presses after S:CE, a concept
I call "Strike: Round Ends", makes an interesting house rule, one that
prevents S:CE cards from becoming too powerful in a limited-card
environment where other S:CE counters are not prevalent. It also has the
interesting effect of making press-based combat viable, which is almost
never true otherwise. This is, IMHO, a far better solution than imposing
a card limit, with respect to solving the problems faced by new
playgroups.)

-- John Whelan

I'm not LSJ but I do know you can use Pscyche in superior to begin a
new combat after the combat end card is played. (I play mostly killer
combat decks...)Certain vamps also have the ability to start a new
combat...

Also a card like Riposte can be used an the damage will be dealth even
if a combat end card is played.

There are ways around combat end (immortal grapple. psyche, riposte...)
